title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.36). Fix an ambient set L. A 'figure' is a pair (S,T), where S ⊂ L and T is an 'ultra-topology' on S. An ultra-topology is what is now called an Alexandrov topology: arbitrary unions of closed sets are closed, and every point has a smallest (open) neighbourhood. Equivalently, T is a preorder on S, with closed sets the down-sets (or up-sets, depending on convention).

Compatibility. Two figures (S,T) and (S',T') are compatible if three conditions hold:
- T and T' induce the same topology on S∩S';
- S∩S' is closed in S for T;
- S∩S' is closed in S' for T'.

Gluing. Given compatibility, this page states there is a unique topology on S∪S' ≅ S ⊔_{S∩S'} S' that induces T on S and T' on S', and for which S and S' are closed. It is the final topology for the two inclusions S → S∪S' and S' → S∪S': A is closed iff A∩S is closed in S and A∩S' is closed in S'.

Bracketed NB. For a family of topological spaces (S_i,T_i) with maps f_i : S_i → X, the final topology on X has as closed sets the A with f_i^{-1}(A) closed for all i. In the present case S∪S' is the amalgamated sum (pushout) of S and S' along their common closed subspace, 'opération topologique bien familière'. Grothendieck started to write that the final topology is again an ultra-topology, and that its associated preorder is ..., then crossed both out.

Subfigures. When S' ⊂ S, the pair is compatible (i.e. (S',T') is a sub-figure of (S,T)) iff S' is closed in (S,T) and T' is the induced topology. So the sub-figures of (S,T) are exactly the closed subsets of S with the induced topology.

Two order relations.
- (S',T') ≪ (S,T) means S' ⊂ S and the inclusion is continuous, i.e. monotone for the associated preorders.
- On the next page, ≼ means S' = S and T' is finer than T.

The purpose is to set up an 'algebra of figures': a combinatorial calculus of gluing, sub-objects and refinement for preorder-structured subsets of a fixed set L. It prepares the next page's problem: classify refinements τ' of a topology τ on S that restrict to a prescribed finer topology τ0' on a closed subset T.
errors: No mathematical errors. Gluing check: with A closed iff A∩S and A∩S' are closed, S is closed because S∩S' is closed in S'. The induced topology on S is T because, for B closed in S, B∩S' = B∩(S∩S') is closed in S∩S' (the topologies agree there), hence closed in S'. Uniqueness follows because a finite closed cover determines the topology.

The crossed-out claim that the final topology of a family of Alexandrov spaces is Alexandrov is in fact true: preimages commute with arbitrary unions. Its associated preorder is the transitive closure of the images of the preorders. The deletion seems to be a decision not to digress, not a retraction of a false claim.
Minor slip: the NB says 'topologie finale sur S' where it should say 'sur X'.

ideas.what: Figures as subsets of a fixed set L equipped with an Alexandrov ('ultra') topology / preorder
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Alexandroff (1937); finite spaces: McCord, Stong (1966)

ideas.what: Gluing two compatible figures along a common closed subspace as a pushout / final topology
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of topological spaces along closed embeddings; closed-cover gluing lemma

ideas.what: Sub-figures = closed subsets with the induced topology (down-sets of the preorder)
ideas.modern_name: Closed subspaces / sieves (down-closed subsets) of a poset

ideas.what: Order relations on figures: ≪ (subset with continuous inclusion) and ≼ (same set, finer topology)
ideas.modern_name: Lattice of topologies / poset of preorder refinements

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine general topology for Alexandrov spaces: gluing along closed subspaces, sub-figures as closed subsets, and refinement orders. It is preparatory bookkeeping for the 1986 'Algèbre des figures', with no new result or connection on this page.
